name: Sapphire Seeker
entries: {@i Component: dragon (sapphire) heart}

Freely floating inside a 1-inch sphere of crystal is an intricately faceted sapphire; a spinning top imbued with swathes of divination magic. When this compass is activated, the top whirls at breakneck speed in a dazzling azure cyclone, before coming to a stop with unerring precision.

name: Sawbones' Bonesaw
entries: {@i Component: giant tooth}

Speckled with rust and blood, this magical saw has a wickedly keen, serrated edge. It is said to be the instrument of choice of back alley doctors and black market suppliers. Amputation operations can be conducted almost instantaneously; plenty of time before the town guard started sticking their nose in.

name: Scalestriker
entries: {@i Component: pouch of monstrosity (merrow) scales}

Scales, be they from the lowly snake or mighty dragon, appear to quail at this blade's presence, peeling back to reveal the flesh below. The hilt's squamous wrapping multiplies slowly, detaching in patches to crawl across the blade's glassy face, and falling lifelessly to the floor after touching its gem-like edge.

name: Scarf of Winter
entries: {@i Component: fey (Jorfraust) hair}

In windy weather, the crystals dangling from this scarf chime softly, producing a sombre yet peaceful winter tune that evokes images of delicate snowflakes colliding against one another during a gentle snowfall. After the crystals have shattered, the absence of their song can be somewhat off-putting.

Scatterguns are similar to muskets in that they are muzzle-loaded and must be reloaded after each shot. They are similarly flintlock weapons, but instead of a single ball they fire buckshot—a grouping of tiny pellets that spread out over a wide area.

name: Scepter of the Unanointed
entries: Centuries ago, a priest named Arbalest the Wise acquired a scepter from a deva for his faith. The angel instructed Arbalest to use the divine instrument to anoint and protect the rulers of Arbalest's now-forgotten kingdom. When Bernasatrix, a powerful demon, possessed the body of a monarch, Arbalest was charged to banish the menace. After five days of failed attempts, the priest retreated to his sanctum and petitioned the spirits of his faith for a solution. Through his prayers, the priest learned to confront the demon in its domain, where the mind and soul meet.

Arbalest and his acolytes banished Bernasatrix into the scepter. The priest kept the item in a secure crypt dedicated to the deva who had gifted the divine rod. As the years passed, the scepter's care was passed to Arbalest's successors within the faith, though their order eventually faded into the tapestries of history, leaving Bernasatrix in lonely, silent fury. The demon vowed to escape one day to exact revenge on Arbalest and the order of his faith.

entries.name: Cleansing the Scepter
entries: To cleanse the scepter of its curse, Bernasastrix must be removed from the item, which requires the wielder to complete a series of trials that Bernasastrix attempts to manipulate.

If asked about the curse, Bernasastrix plays the role of benevolent spirit and notes three holy sites where Arbalest once taught, studied, and prayed, claiming that destroying heretic iconographies at each site will lift the curse. This is a lie—the sites are connected to Arbalest's order. Damage or destruction would weaken the divine magic binding the demon spirit to the scepter and allow them to escape, which destroys the item and ends the character's curse.

In truth, the wielder must instead recite and meditate on the fifteen virtues of Arbalest's faith in each site. Once this ritual is completed, the scepter is cleansed, Bernastrix is destroyed, and the item loses its Sentience and Curse properties.

entries.name: The Fifteen Virtues of Arbalest
entries: Arbalest's faith has fifteen virtues that serve as central tenets of their beliefs.

items.name: Acceptance
entries: Welcome any and all to the faith.

items.name: Authenticity
entries: Be true to yourself and your faith.

items.name: Caring
entries: Care for others, always.

items.name: Commitment
entries: Keep all promises, oaths, and agreements.

items.name: Compassion
entries: Ease all pain in others.

items.name: Courage
entries: All have the strength to persevere against any hardship.

items.name: Fairness
entries: Faith has no favoritism.

items.name: Forgiveness
entries: All can be forgiven with time.

items.name: Honesty
entries: Speak the truth whenever possible.

items.name: Hope
entries: Inspire others to achieve the impossible.

items.name: Humility
entries: All are equal in faith; none are above another.

items.name: Peace
entries: A calm heart is an open one.

items.name: Respect
entries: Honor others, not for wisdom or gains, but for their being.

items.name: Thankfulness
entries: Always be thankful, for life is short.

items.name: Wisdom
entries: Learning is a lifelong journey.
You can substitute any virtue with another that best suits your narrative or setting.

entries.name: Cleansed
entries: When the Scepter of the Unanointed is cleansed of its curse, it gains the following properties:

entries.name: Charitable
entries: When you cast a spell using the rod's Anointed Spells property, you can target one additional creature within the spell's range.

entries.name: Selfless
entries: Whenever a creature you can see within 60 feet of you is reduced to 0 hit points while you are holding this rod, you can use a reaction to stabilize the target. Once you use this property, it can't be used again until the next dawn, unless you expend a spell slot of 4th level or higher to use it again.

entries.name: Anointment
entries: You add {@spell holy aura} spell to the list of spells that can be cast using the rod's Anointed Spells property. When cast from the rod, the spell has a range of a creature you can touch.

images.altText: A golden scepter with a winged sphere at the head Golden seraph wings emerge top and bottom from the sphere, which is embossed with rubies and images of rearing lions.

name: Sceptre of the Spellcrafter
entries: {@i Component: elemental primordial dust}

This gold and onyx length of wood is ornately carved with the likeness of black dragon, and houses four large gemstones: a ruby, emerald, sapphire, and diamond. Each gem flickers with an inner light, a core of elemental magic. Blending evocation and transmutation magic, this device allows the destructive forces of the elements to be shaped to the whim of its wielder.

name: Sceptre of the Sunken King
entries: {@i Component: aberration tentacle}

An ancient nautilus, a scion of the Deep One, wraps the driftwood shaft of this sceptre in its wet, rubbery tentacles. Though this nautilus appears dead and unmoving when dry, its tentacles slowly writhe while submerged in water.

name: Sceptre of the Sunken King (Very Rare)
Scionic Armament
entries: The Scions' weapons—whether dead or alive—are constructed from the bones of formidable monsters which are then tortured with strong lightning, granting twisted appearance and savage fury to the armament. The weapon's osseous component grants it ancient strength, and the electricity that dances across its body brutalizes all who come in contact with it.
Scionic weapons all require attunement. When attuning to such a weapon, a creature takes {@damage 2d8} lightning damage.

items.name: Reminder:
entries: Forced movement does not trigger {@action Opportunity Attack|PHB|opportunity attacks}

name: Scorch Helm
entries: {@i Component: elemental core of fire}

The golden flames adorning this helmet produce as much heat as a raging inferno, but somehow never harm their wearer or their allies. Many speculate that they are fueled by the wearer's passion and emotions, flaring at times of great anger, excitement, or distress.

name: Scorching Fists
entries: {@i Component: phial of construct oil}

Made of ceramic and metal plating, these gloves allow their wearer to smelt, weld, and otherwise manipulate metal without fear of burning oneself. In underground battle pits, these gloves see more unconventional uses: with the limiters removed, the glove's knuckle-exhausts can form blades of devastating flame.

name: Scorching Wrath
entries: {@i Component: pouch of monstrosity (remorhaz) teeth}
Within this sharp-edged bone dagger lies an inert lump of indigo obsidian. In the heat of battle, the obsidian erupts into a continual flow of molten stone to which you are impervious.

name: Scroll of Fungi
entries: {@i Component: pouch of plant hyphae}

From morel to flycap, pixie's parasol to displacer's digestif, this magical vellum parchment sprouts an assortment of new mushrooms with each new dawn. Its true power, however, is in summoning magic mushrooms. To those without knowledge of the required languages, the letters on the scroll shift and move, seemingly without meaning.

name: Scythe of the Headless Seahorseman
entries: {@i Component: beast (giant sea horse) fin}
This rusted scythe, with its driftwood handle that supports a plethora of sea life, is surprisingly light and hydrodynamic.

name: Scythe of the Headless Seahorseman (Very Rare)
Sea Serpent's Tooth
entries: {@i Component: pouch of dragon teeth}
Carved from the tooth of a giant sea snake, this huge club sports a thriving ecosystem of halophilic moss, barnacles, and seaweed.

name: Seam Ripper
entries: {@i Component: Undead (Chrysalich) Ethereal Ichor}
As I've always said, any skilled and precise seamstress will pin her enemies down before sowing their destruction.

name: Seashell Weapon
entries: {@i Component: beast fin}
Fashioned from the pearlescent bloodshells of the Scarlet Reef, this weapon of the coralborn is enchanted to be especially hydrodynamic underwater.

name: Ser Boncou Rage
entries: {@i Component: monstrosity (shapechanger) liver}

Dealing with lycanthropy, curses from the Far Realms, or mutations caused by the sentient, self replicating Mut-X mutagen can jade even the most resilient nurse of the Night Hospitaller. These potions of bottled courage, all of which go by the name Ser Boncou Rage, can imbue a terrified sister with the immense determination required to cure lycanthropy on a full moon or protect them from the wiles of an especially charming vampire.

name: Serpent Bladewhip
entries: {@note Original idea by Rebecca Verrall}
Slithering silver strikes, swiftly severing sinister shadows.

entries.name: Seven-Ringed Cup
entries: The treasure is a chalice made of indestructible bronze, formed into the shape of a heptagon. Each side is intricately carved with decorative flairs, depicting abstract triangular shapes and seven-leafed flowers.

entries.name: Seven-Ringed Cup
entries: The treasure is a chalice made of indestructible bronze, formed into the shape of a heptagon. Each side is intricately carved with decorative flairs, depicting abstract triangular shapes and seven-leafed flowers.

name: Sevenfold Reaper
entries: {@i Component: pouch of plant leaves}

Most people would agree that adding more blades to a sword gives diminishing returns on efficacy. Some would consider three blades to be enough. Many would stop at five. Almost all would see no point in more than ten. These people are simpletons and fools who ignore the truth: you can never have too many blades.

name: Shadow Mamba Venom
entries: The venom of an {@creature emerald shadow mamba|TPK} retains its potency for up to a year outside the snake. While dangerous, a shadow mamba can be milked for three doses of venom every week. Doing so requires a successful DC 23 Wisdom ({@skill Animal Handling}) check against an {@condition incapacitated} mamba. A single dose can be extracted from a dead {@creature emerald shadow mamba|TPK} with minimal effort (and a great deal less risk).

name: Shadowsheath
entries: {@i Component: Celestial (Morphelean) Skin}

This sword is like an onion; it has layers. Specifically, it has a terrifying demonic sheath layer, a glimmering celestial blade layer, and then a juicy core of uncontrollable, frenzied rage, all wrapped in a sheath of devilish smoke.

name: Shadowstalker Garb
entries: {@i Component: construct instructions}

This mechanical garb was tailor-made to allow assassins to glide over their target without being heard, before eliminating them with a swift, swooping attack. Anton Spark, the famous tinkerer, modelled this design after a snowy owl silently snatched a doughnut from his hand.

name: Shakwraps
entries: {@i Component: Beast Chitin}

A true warrior will always welcome the respectful salute of a fellow combatant. Those who flee the salute are probably dishonourable. They should be chakram'd and their life force absorbed the moment they turn their backs.

name: Shard of Moonlight
entries: This weapon is the flesh of a Great One carved away in pain and fashioned into a blade. The Shard of Moonlight is the reason the Shattered Moon exists and the Devouring Moon is no more. He who wields the blade is overwhelmed by hope, however misguided it might be...

name: Sharktooth
entries: {@i Component: pouch of beast (giant shark) teeth}
Fashioned especially for the Hammerhead Knight, this blade caused its victims to bleed, allowing the knight, with its superior sense of smell, to track a would-be assassin back to its lair.

name: Shield of Retaliation
entries: {@i Component: fiend heart}

Legend says that when the war twixt fiends and celestials ravaged the Material Plane, a great infernal general had these shields forged for his captains. Through them he observed the battlefield, and with them he smote the angels that dared challenge his armies. Whether or not the fiendish general still watches through these shields, or even still lives, is a question yet to be answered.

An upgrade from scatterguns, shotguns have two barrels, are breach-loaded, and are set off by a hammer instead of a flint. They are additionally more reliable and hit harder, and this extra bit of craftsmanship generally makes them more expensive as well.

name: Shrimp Pistol
entries: {@i Component: pouch of aberration claws}
A biomantic fusion of crustacean and firearm, this magic weapon thrums with stored energy, ready to release a devastating strike like its pistol shrimp namesake.

name: Shroud of Ending
entries: There is an old tale about a foolish birdfolk sage who believed themselves to be even wiser than the Amaranthine. One day, while wandering alone in the Wood at night, they met Tyton, who had come to collect their soul. Rather than accept their death with dignity, the sage instead debated with {@deity Tyton|Amaranthine|HumblewoodCampaignSetting} about the unfairness of mortality. {@deity Tyton|Amaranthine|HumblewoodCampaignSetting} could not deny their logic, but warned the heedless sage about disrupting the cycle of life and death. He wove a cloak from the fabric of the night sky itself, infused it with a small fraction of his power, and gifted it to the sage. With this, the sage could live forever. {@deity Tyton|Amaranthine|HumblewoodCampaignSetting} declared that he would return in a century, and if the sage still felt the same, the Amaranthine of death would never again visit them. For a hundred years, the sage watched everyone around them gradually age, succumbing to illness and death as they lived on. In the end, the sage understood their folly and asked for {@deity Tyton|Amaranthine|HumblewoodCampaignSetting} to guide them peacefully into the hereafter. It is said that {@deity Tyton|Amaranthine|HumblewoodCampaignSetting} left the Shroud of Ending in the world as a reminder of the sage's foolishness.

name: Silkspun Lantern
entries: {@i Component: fey (moth) egg}

This enchanting lantern stirs a deep fascination in the hearts of those who behold it, and can be used to lure unsuspecting humanoids to the Plane of Fey. Weak-willed creatures who so much as glance at its mesmerising lilac hues find themselves haunted by wistful memories of its light and a desire to be near it.

name: Singularity
entries: {@i Component: aberration brain}
With a thought, this staff opens up a tiny portal to the event horizon of a black hole, moulding the warped space-time into a spearhead of flickering force energy.

name: Sins
entries: Sins are a form of "item modification", a modular way of adding to the properties an item possesses. In return for completing a sinful task appointed by a fiend, a creature can attune to—or enhance their attunement to—a magic item, which gains a powerful new property.

entries.name: The Task
entries: A fiend's ultimate goal with a task is to form a contract with a player character; they give the character powers and request that a specific task be performed within a certain time limit (GM's choice). If the task is completed, the item retains the property for the duration of the character's attunement to it. If the task isn't completed within the time limit (including being failed outright), the character's soul is forfeit, and the GM may choose what infernal outcome awaits the character. The tasks are always secret; if the recipient of the task willingly or unwillingly divulges information about its task to any other creature, the creature automatically fails the task. The tasks accompanying each sin are just suggestions—feel free to come up with your own tasks.

entries.name: Rarity & Power
entries: The sins scale using rarity, with more powerful boons being granted at higher rarities. The greater the item's rarity (and therefore its power), the more extreme and unpleasant the task should be; the fiend wants the character to fail! In general, it is advisable to match the sin rarity to the item rarity.

entries.name: Optional or Enhanced Attunement
entries: If the item wouldn't usually require attunement, then the addition of this item modification gives the item the "optional attunement" property; a character who completes the assigned task immediately attunes to the item, which gains a new property (usually named after the sin in question). If the item already requires attunement, then a creature that accepts the devil's task can't willingly unattuned from the item for the duration of the task. When the task is completed, the item becomes enhanced with the new property.

Either way, the item's new property persists for as long as the character remains attuned to the item; if the character loses attunement to the item for any reason, it must accept and complete a new task to regain the property.

name: Sir Wrenchinald the Third
entries: {@i Component: fey psyche}

name: Skinchanger Arm Ring
entries: This arm ring is made from copper and is covered with a patina that cannot be removed.

There was once a sect of Northern warriors dedicated to learning from the animals in their region. Each member of the order sought to exemplify the capabilities and spirit of their chosen animal. The raven warrior was keen to observe and could travel far and fast. The follower of the wolf fought well in conjunction with others. Others had strength and endurance like bears.

These ideals were forged into an enchanted arm ring worn by the leader of the sect. Whether this magic was achieved with the aid of dwarves, druids, or sorcerers, none can say. With experience, the wearer of the arm ring could shapeshift into one of the three animals exemplified by the warriors.

Though the order won many victories on the battlefield, they couldn't be held in the employ of any one jarl. The wilds called to them, and they visited the settled lands of the North less and less as the years went by, until they were never seen again.

name: Skinwalker Staff
entries: {@i Component: beast pelt}
Used in shamanistic rituals to commune with wildlife, this staff is adorned with animal skulls and bones.

name: Skuld of the Valkyries
entries: A valkyrie's body and equipment typically vanish when the creature is slain. However, if a {@creature shield maiden|TPK} is defeated by an enemy it greatly respects, it may choose to leave behind its mighty tower shield.

Oh! Oh gods, are you seriously asking me to explain it? Geez, sure, I'll try, but you really gotta feel it, you know? The sensation of the wind whipping past you as you shoot up into the sky, then—whoa!—your stomach just drops out from you, and it's like you left your heart behind as you start to fall. It's like nothing's holding onto you, then—whoosh!—the wind catches you, and swings you back into the sky.

images.altText: An Ashari woman with long orange hair flies on her white-winged skysail through a rocky canyon. She wears green clothing.
A skyship, its white sails entirely unfurled, flies through a dusky, red sky. The ship emanates a glowing, blue arcane magic below it, keeping it aloft.

name: Sleuth's Shadowcoat
entries: {@i Component: undead (shadow) ethereal ichor}

Sometimes, a detective's best tool is remaining undetected. The sleuth's shadowcoat allows its wearer to take full advantage of shadows, to hide in plain sight, and to disappear in a puff of smoke (well... fog) when things go awry. Also, it has plenty of secret and obvious pockets in which to store things. Very useful.

Sniper rifles are essentially hunting rifles that have been machined to a higher degree of precision and quality. This results in better range, damage, but also more weight and skill to craft, and they can often be very difficult to find.

Even rarer than its single-shot brother, the revolver sniper rifle operates on the same principles, but carries four cartridges in revolving chambers, allowing for faster follow-up shots and less time spent reloading.

name: Snow Wolf Cowl
entries: {@i Component: monstrosity (winter wolf) pelt}

Few warriors can claim to have single-handedly bested a full-grown snow wolf. Those that do can have the head of such a monster enchanted by a clan shaman, granting them the power to transform into the beast. Such cowls are prized trophies amongst the frozen Norse clans, symbols of might and status.

entries.name: Solomon's Knowledge
entries: The treasure is a rolled scroll made of simple white parchment, sealed with red wax.

entries.name: Solomon's Knowledge
entries: The treasure is a rolled scroll made of simple white parchment, sealed with red wax.

name: Solstice Needle
entries: At the core of a {@creature lynchwood|TPK} is its heartwood, a dense and durable wood shaped by the befouled energies of the {@creature lynchwood|TPK}'s red-hot soul. The heartwood is dark, appearing almost ashen and charred, with faint lines of green running through it. It can be used to create a spellcasting focus called a solstice needle. Creating a solstice needle from a {@creature lynchwood|TPK}'s heartwood requires a successful DC 22 Wisdom ({@item Carpenter's Tools|PHB}) check. On a failure, the heartwood is mangled and becomes worthless.

name: Solstice Star
entries: By their very nature, voidborn leave little behind when they are slain. Their bodies collapse into nothingness, fading into the void that gave them life. The death of a voidborn—and the resulting collapse in the void—can sometimes cause an upswelling of magic as the weave rushes in, and in these cases, a solstice star is formed. This tiny sphere offers protections against magic and from the energies of the void, and they are held in high regard by spellcasters and those who hunt voidborn. Such individuals would pay 15,000 gp for a solstice star.

name: Soulkeeper Pendant
entries: {@i Component: phial of celestial blood}
Tools of devilish origin, these mundane-looking miniature animal skulls are designed to increase the throughput of souls to the Hells.

name: Sparkblade
entries: {@i Component: dragon (blue or bronze) breath sac}
As arcanodynamos have become more common, there has been an explosion in devices making use of this magic-generating technology. From lanterns to rollerskates, and now: sparkblades.

name: Speak No Evil
entries: {@i Component: giant tooth}
This headgear - a gag consisting of two leaden 'hands' connected by thick leather straps - is designed to make speech impossible.

name: Spear of the Stormsinger
entries: {@i Component: dragon (blue or bronze) breath sac}

Stormsingers—disciples of the Allfather—are said to be able to channel the wrath of storms into holy weapons. If one of their sacred sites is threatened, the air is filled with a berserker's chant as they throw themselves into combat with a zealousness inspired by the prospect of entry into the Allfather's halls.

name: Spellbreaker
entries: {@i Component: magical material - cold iron}

In the Sylvan language, the word for "cold iron" roughly translates to "joy-sapper", as many fey and magical creatures consider this metal to be cruel and unnatural, draining the magic and whimsy from the world. Simply carrying anything made from it is highly taboo amongst most fey courts, and likely to earn their immediate distrust and contempt.

name: Spellsling
entries: {@i Component: phial of humanoid (spellcaster) blood}

"Why should spell scrolls only be usable by those who've learned to cast spells?" During her brief tenure as wizard de-punification coach at the Academia Magicalis, Heliana commissioned this magical slingshot so that she, too, could do the magically sparkly things.

Records kept by the Birthheart temple in Vasselheim say that the Spire of Conflux was created when the Wildmother breathed on a young beech tree. The sapling transformed into a curving staff and the Wildmother's breath crystallized into the glowing jewel that hovers in its center. The bearer of this mythic staff can command the elements as if they were one with the enduring, yet ever-changing, landscape of Exandria itself...

images.altText: A twisted staff made of wood and vines shaped like a shepherd's crook with a glowing blue crystal in the center of the crook.

name: Spiritual Armblade
entries: {@i Component: celestial hair}
These magical prostheses were gifted to the warrior-servants of the divine in recompense for limbs lost in battle.

name: Springwing
entries: {@i Component: pouch of fey feathers}

To create this scimitar, the sumptuous feathers of fey creatures are dipped in molten metal and thereafter shaped and sharpened to create small steel swallows. The swallows describe complex and hypnotising patterns in the air as they fly around the blade, and the screech produced by the beating of their wings resembles the cacophonous chirping of dozens of birds.

name: Staff of Decay
entries: {@i Component: plant membrane}

A softly luminescent, magical fungus grows at the tip of this staff, constantly draining small amounts of positive energy from its surroundings. In its presence, plants lose a little of their colour and droop ever so slightly, but these effects are only temporary and quickly fade when the staff is no longer around.

Many weapons created by mortals during the Age of Arcanum were designed with hopes to surpass or even destroy the gods, but not so with Dwueth'var. That shining sword, bright with the light of the bold full moon and the enigmatic starlit night, was forged by acolytes of the Wildmother and the Moonweaver, united in their love of this fragile world and their determination to protect it.

images.altText: A silver greatsword with a red hilt. Inset in the hilt is a green gemstone. Runes run down the center of the blade, where also runs silver-white lines of magic.

name: Starfallen Force Shield
entries: {@i Component: elemental primordial dust}

The Starfallen are a sect of astronautical zealots sworn to prevent the incursion of aberrations from the far reaches of the universe. Though they are unknown to most folk on the Material Plane, it is their vigilance which ensures the relative normality the plane's denizens can enjoy. The force shield is one of their astral armaments, designed to disarm and incapacitate foes.

name: Starforged Weapon
entries: {@i Component: pouch of fiend dust}

With an enormous array of mirrors (and a touch of magic), starlight can be focussed to such an intensity that the iron within a trapped comet can be gradually wrought into any shape. Such metal is known as starforged iron and is imbued with a unique property that activates as a creature moves towards or away from its target.

name: Starrunner's Twinblade
entries: {@i Component: aberration brain}

An astral raider deprived of their dragon needs to travel light. The starrunner's twinblade is the ideal, multifunctional tool; a devastating blade, bow, and shield rolled into one. With such a diverse weapon, one can hunt food, clear a watering hole, and defend oneself, all while retaining mobility.

name: Stellar Remnant
entries: {@i Component: magical material - cosmic iron}

Birthed in the last gasp of a dying star, the raw material of stellar remnant was discovered inside condensed space dust that fell from the stars as a meteor. Breaking up upon colliding with the atmosphere (and an unlucky dragon), the meteor's fragments have since been reforged as several weapons that can channel the power of their progenitor star, now a black hole, to exert overbearing amounts of gravitational force.

name: Stheno's Bow
entries: {@i Component: monstrosity (medusa) eye}

The first of these bows was found in the abandoned lair of an ancient medusa who preferred to slaughter her victims rather than turning them to stone. After years of meticulous reverse engineering, L'Arsène Upin was able to recreate its ophidian enchantments, and each of the resulting bows bears the name of its original creator, who has yet to be found.
Why?
In the brazen fury of the hunt, you may lose your weapon and need to reach for something to defend yourself. Sometimes it's useful. Sometimes it's a stick

name: Stickaxe
entries: {@i Component: Phial of Ooze (Splatacabra) Mucus}

No matter how many times the sludge oozing from this weapon is scraped off or washed away, the blade and haft are quickly covered again. When its inventor, Thomumin Underjaw, was asked what to do with the excess, he said, "I've tried burning it, eating it, freezing it, and making bouncy balls for small children. None of that worked, so it's your problem now."

name: Storm's Eye
entries: {@i Component: elemental volatile mote of air}

Storm's eye houses a miniaturised storm ripped from the Elemental Plane of Air, which it channels to produce a blade of erratic lightning. Ever since the artificer Elbert Ainstein received a shock from such a weapon, leaving him with permanently static hair, such blades come with a warning to wear rubber gloves when wielding them.

name: Storrbani
entries: Thogar Giant-Hewer earned great renown through unwavering bravery but not intellectual brilliance. His unmatched courage often forged far ahead of his reason. As a youth, he could not prevent marauding giants and trolls from destroying his village and murdering his family. Left alone on the blood-soaked snow, a fire kindled deep in Thogar's heart. From that day, he unwaveringly sought vengeance against giantfolk, not for glory or renown but in the hope his daring might earn him friends or even a new family of his own.

The Giant-Hewer became a terror to trolls and giants alike. Though not the strongest warrior and certainly never the wisest, he braved troll dens and giant camps, throwing himself into battle where others paused to strategize. Yet time and again, the people he saved turned cold. His deeds, though brave, were rarely welcome. His plans resulted in the death of everyone but himself. His traps lured giants to their doom at the expense of entire villages. Those he rescued offered no feasts of thanks, only wary glances and closed doors. The more he gave, the more alone he became, yet still he fought on believing if he was only brave enough, he could win through to find a new family.

Thogar met his end in his own typical fashion. After running across the trail of a band of storm giants heading toward a village, he foolishly attacked them in the settlement square. His blade, Storrbani, slew many giants before the others fled, but unfortunately, the fires ignited by the battle burned down half the village. Thogar's shattered body lay in the remains of the wedding feast (to which the giants had been invited), and no one came to his aid or to witness his last breath. Skalds say he died utterly alone, but when the Valkyries came to collect him, he did not wish to enter Valhalla alone. Taking pity on the brave warrior, they cast his spirit into his blade, binding it there until the day he falls again, fighting beside a true friend, so together they might enter the Hall of Golden Shields side by side.

name: Stungunblade
entries: {@i Component: construct (divine-infused) arcanothermic core}

You've heard of magical firearms built seamlessly into sharp swords. You've heard of guns created to incapacitate rather than kill. But the combination of those could only ever come from the brilliant mind of Branton Quark, to whom the word "can't" is a challenge, and the word "shouldn't", tantamount to blasphemy.

name: Summoner's Sickle
entries: {@i Component: fiend (imp) bone}

From the bones of imps and other fiends, this osseous sickle thrums with magic from the schools of necromancy and conjuration. The skulls that ornament the blade chatter and clack at the taste of blood, as if yearning to clamber free of their posthumous embrace.

name: Sun-Cursed Blood
entries: {@creature Sun-cursed|TPK} have magic-infused blood that is of great value to spellcasters and warriors. Extracting the blood of a {@creature sun-cursed|TPK} requires a successful DC 20 Wisdom ({@skill Medicine}) check and yields one vial of blood per {@creature sun-cursed|TPK}. A vial of blood can be sold for 1,000 gp, and the bodies of the Nartheneen {@creature sun-cursed|TPK} are worth 18,000 gp, though selling either blood or bodies attracts significant negative attention from all other Nartheneen.

name: Sundial Ring
entries: {@i Component: fey (sunsprite) antenna}

Attuned to the movement of the sun in the sky by intricate enchantments, this ring functions even when kept away from the light, serving as a lifeline to the warmth and brightness of day. In the deepest caverns and darkest dungeons, it reminds brave adventurers that the light shines upon them always.

name: Suneater Axe
entries: {@i Component: pouch of celestial teeth}

When the mighty wolf Fenrir threatened the world, the dwarves fashioned an impossibly strong thread with which to keep him bound. This thread, known as Gleipnir, was crafted from the sound of a cat's footfall, the roots of a mountain, and the breath of a fish, amongst other things. With the leftover material, the Weapons of Binding were made. The suneater axe is one such weapon, a depiction of the wolf Sköll, who the dwarves believe will one day devour the sun.

name: Sunken Anchor
entries: {@i Component: monstrosity antler}
Covered in flakes of blue-green bronze and barnacles, this sturdy implement looks like it's seen better days.

name: Sunken Slasher
entries: {@i Component: elemental volatile mote of water}

The unusual shape and nature of these weapons have been matters of debate for experts the world over. Why fashion them from unwieldy anchors? Why are they found at the bottom of oceans? Why place the ring at the tip of the swords? Meanwhile, several storm giant children bemoan the loss of their bubble blowing toys.

name: Sunsplitter
entries: {@i Component: elemental core of fire}

It is said that, in order to forge a connection with the sun, each step of this weapon's creation must be carried out exclusively in its bright light, during the hottest days of the year. Whether or not all crafters follow this practice, there's no denying the command that the wielder of this spear holds over the sun's radiant beams.

name: Tableturner
entries: {@i Component: construct (divine-infused) instructions}

Sometimes, even a star needs a little help to shine bright. Flip the world of music on its head with Quark Industries' brand new tableturnerTM, and discover the 'hex factor' that's been inside of you all along. With the tableturnerTM, you'll never need another instrument again.

name: Tail of the Mermalia
entries: {@i Component: beast fin}

When the rakin ousted Dr. Stein from his tower, he had only one means of escape: swim. His last act in the battle was to sever his own legs, attune to the tail, flop into a well, and slink out into the sea, tail between his... well. He didn't have legs anymore.

name: Tails of Glory
entries: {@i Component: Monstrosity (Mantiroar) Stinger}

Originally called "Sit on Your Grass," this prosthesis was designed with tensioned blades to easily mow stretches of lawn. Poor initial sales and multiple complaints of the blades' rapid, spontaneous deconstruction led to a recall, redesign, and rebranding, targeting the adventurer demographic instead.

name: Tainted Edge
entries: When a {@creature rakshasa yoddha|TPK} is defeated in honorable combat, it bursts into flames, leaving behind a trophy for the victor(s) to keep. This gift is always one of the yoddha's blades, a greatsword fashioned of green steel that is tainted with the very essence of evil.

name: Taz's Zealous Retribution
entries: {@i Component: construct lifespark}

A common field tool, the TZR, as it is referred to by FBI agents, is the creation of the Bureau's very own inventor: Tazon Regalton. Designed primarily for incapacitating fleeing evil-doers, the TZR also packs a punch when necessary.

name: Technomancer Staff
entries: {@i Component: elemental core of air}

name: That-Which-Hungers
entries: {@i Component: aberration brain}

A dark entity reaches out from within this blade that it calls home, its hungry voice echoing painfully in your head. As its gluttonous presence invades your mind, like a hundred slithering tentacles caressing your brain, one word rings out above the rest: "SUGAR".

name: The Crystalliser
entries: {@i Component: magical material - planar bismuth}

Planar bismuth is highly sought after by two very distinct groups: the chaotic fey are transfixed by its beautiful rainbow iridescence, while inhabitants of the lawful Outer Planes admire the orderly nature of its crystalline structure. Violent feuds tend to break out as these two factions vie for control of the rare crystals, which they often weaponise to battle one another.

entries.name: Harvesting - Planar Bismuth
entries: Planar bismuth is a metal found only outside of the Material Plane, usually in areas where the barriers between planes are thinner. It has a component DC of 15 and has no time limit in which it needs to be harvested. However, planar bismuth is highly sought after, and when you try to harvest it, there's a 25% chance you come across a random encounter, usually consisting of hostile fey or constructs.

name: The Grave Blade
entries: The reavers of Wolfheim brought home many strange treasures as souvenirs and mementos from their campaigns abroad. A dwarven warrior named Essalla claimed a strange sword as her share of the spoils on one such raiding journey. Unusual in design and unadorned by dwarvish standards, it seemed destined to be a souvenir brought out only when tales of the campaign were to be told.
This sword has a dull, lifeless grey blade, and the hilt is carved from aged bone. The guard is made from ribs, and the pommel is sourced from the rounded end of a femur, both cast in bronze

The Grave Blade became known in different tales, for the threads of fate of each bearer seemed to be cut short soon after taking possession of it. It has changed hands many times over the next nine years, seemingly taken from a corpse as often as it was exchanged for gold or favors.

The blade is known for the song it hums in the presence of undead, and with the death of its carriers, the blade's song grows ever more insistent. Some say the song is a warning, while others theorize that it wants to be found and interred with the body of its first bearer.

The souvenir of so much death was lost among a merchant's wares that never reached their destination in Wolfheim, and the mystery of its song persists in tales told on dark nights when the fire burns low.

name: The Steamer (rare)
entries: {@i Component: Aberration (Chuulverin) Chitin}
You call chuuls steamed lobsters?
Yes! It's a... regional dialect.
Uh-huh. What region?
Uh... Upper Voidsea.
entries.by: Conversation between Admiral Chalmers and Captain Skinner

name: The Sword out of the Stone

images.title: The Sword out of the Stone

name: The Sword out of the Stone

images.title: The Sword out of the Stone

name: The Uplifter
entries: {@i Component: elemental volatile mote of fire}

Devised by a pair of mischievous magical students, this firework has been banned from nearly all major learning institutions. Although its intricate magic produces a dazzling array of shapes and colours, its raw explosive power is such that many have taken to using it for more offensive purposes, and its name has taken on a much more literal meaning.

War broke out in heaven. From the throne came flashes of lightning, and rumblings and peals of thunder, and before the throne were burning seven torches of fire. Mikha'el and his angels fought against the dragon, and the dragon and his angels fought back. But he was not strong enough, and they lost their place in heaven. The great dragon was hurled down—that ancient serpent called the devil, who leads the whole world astray. He was hurled to the earth, and his angels with him.

name: Thornbow
entries: {@i Component: plant bark}

Unseelie fey—those with a love for the cold and ugly facets of the world—cultivate the malevolent syklthorn, a green-brown creeper with bright red thorns. Syklthorn is a carnivorous plant that snatches creatures who venture too close before eviscerating them with its bladelike thorns. Weapons made from this plant are just as bloodthirsty.

name: Thurible of the Elder Deacon
entries: {@i Component: aberration fat}
This solid steel incense dispenser dangles at the end of a black metal chain. Heady perfume follows in the wake of the bearer of this weighty weapon.

name: Tidecutter
entries: {@i Component: elemental core of water}

With the sound of waves crashing violently against a rocky cliff, the sword's blade rushes forth like the tide, inevitable and unstoppable. Not even tempered steel can resist its edge, which slices through obstacles like a hot knife through melted butter.

images.credit: One of: Miguel Regodón Harkness, Marcel Mercado, William O'Brien, Sam Perin, Florian Stitz, Bryan Syme, Egil Thompson, Jon Pintar

name: Time in a Bottle
entries: The essence of the {@creature tasey-am|TPK} can be distilled into a potion of incredible power called time in a bottle. This elixir allows the drinker to engage in accelerated action like the {@creature tasey-am|TPK} itself, but it is incredibly difficult to create. A DC 24 Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) ability check is required to harvest the components successfully, and a DC 24 Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}), Intelligence ({@skill History}), or Intelligence ({@skill Nature}) ability check is needed to make the potion. Failure destroys the ingredients. The body of the {@creature tasey-am|TPK} provides just enough essence for one potion—there are no second chances on either check.

entries.name: Description:
entries: The Timekeeper's Orb is a rare artifact intricately linked with the {@creature Timeless Goliath|MaM}. This ancient relic appears as a palm-sized sphere, crafted from the same celestial metal as the Goliath's skin, shimmering with ethereal purples and blues that seem to hold a cosmos within. A golden inlay encircles the orb, mirroring the golden ornaments worn by the Goliath. The Timekeeper's Orb is incredibly dense, reflecting its potent connection with time and space.

name: Titan Feller
entries: {@i Component: giant bone}

It is fitting that these blades are fashioned from the jawbones of giants, for the sight of such a weapon makes the teeth of even the mightiest colossi chatter with fear. Originally built by a halfling clan determined to put an end to the tyranny of stature, these swords are undeniable proof that size isn't a true measure of the power one wields.

images.altText: A pair of solid black stone gauntlets with brass fixings, encircled with three stone rings per gauntlet, and they are engraved with orange glowing runes.

name: Toothy Brawl
entries: {@i Component: Pouch of Fey (Giblin) Teeth}
Everyone's heard the classic threat "I'll punch your teeth in," but few have heard the more upsetting threat of "I'll punch my teeth into you."

name: Topaz Despoiler
entries: {@i Component: dragon (topaz) heart}

The articulated mechanical hand at the tip of this item sporadically animates with bursts of negative energy. The fingers fondly caress the flawless topaz orb fixed to the palm, which pulses hypnotically with a gentle, steady glow.

name: Tordalfr's Rebuttal
entries: Tordalfr was a storm giantkin born to a human mother in a small village. After years of jibes and taunts from the children of local warriors, he snapped.

Brael, son of the village headman, and a pompous, aspiring warrior, called Tordalfr out in public, proclaiming to his assembled cronies that there was irrefutable evidence that Tordalfr was the unwanted child of forbidden lovers, and defying anyone present to offer proof to the contrary.

Tordalfr's fury reached such a pitch that the cloudless sky opened up and a bolt of lightning struck his outstretched hand, coalescing into the form of a throwing spear, which he hurled at his tormentor. The javelin struck Brael in the chest, hurling him backward and leaving a blackened, smoking crater where his heart had been. Tordalfr marched furiously from the village and never returned.

name: Tortuga Cannon
entries: {@i Component: dragon (dragon turtle) heart}

When the fire of a drake-kin meets the briny depths of the ocean, seas broil and kelp writhes with draconic ferocity. Fashioned from the scales of a dragon turtle, this sleeve-like device can produce jets of water with the force of a cannon, scalding and entangling its target.

name: Torture Tincture
entries: {@i Component: monstrosity poison gland}

This two-inch-tall phial of oily liquid has a decidedly untrustworthy air to it. Using its bandage scarf, it can climb up any surface, before depositing a dose of poison in whatever vessel, meal, or concoction its wielder chooses. Stories say such a magical contraption was used to poison a king who'd locked himself in a high tower, and that this was the origin of the veinworm plague.

entries.name: Disclaimer:
entries: Please be advised that while some may use torture as a plot device or as a means of gathering information, it is a sensitive and disturbing topic. While the use of torture can be integral to the story being told, which is why it is included in this book, it is important to ensure that everyone at the table comes to an agreement regarding its use prior to the session beginning, and if it's included, whether descriptions should fade to black or be more detailed.

name: Totally Normal Goose Figurine (Figurine of Wondrous Power)
Translux Candle
entries: {@i Component: aberration fat}

Translux candlewax is refined from the rendered fat of planes-travelling beings. This wax is poured in the centre of a permanent teleportation circle under the light of the stars, causing the resulting candle to become locked to that teleportation circle.

name: Trident of the Electric Eel
entries: {@i Component: pouch of dragon (blue) teeth}
Imbued with the natural lightning-based magic of the eelfolk, this brass-headed, magical trident is enchanted to never succumb to the corrosive nature of the briny sea.

name: Trident of the Electric Eel (Very Rare)

entries: "The weapon known as True Name is inseparable from the history of the Seven Cities. Whenever two devils entered into a deal with one another, the offeree of the contract would seal their true name into its ornamentations, then the blade would remain in the possession of the offerer. Should the offeree fail to uphold their end of the contract, the offerer would magically learn the name from the blade, thus gaining power over they who betrayed the sacred pact.

Is there, thus, any blade with more potential? It is written that if an infernal soul could discover the true name of the weapon itself, they could draw from it every name sworn to it since the blade's creation. Imagine the power that individual would have over the Seven Cities. Imagine the proud devils who could do naught but fall to their knees.
I have sought the blade's name for centuries. With luck, when I find it, its bearer will not know the power they wield, and it will be mine."

entries.name: An Ancient True Name
entries: Since the illrigger has many viable playstyles, {@i True Name}'s shape and rarity are flexible, allowing the GM to bestow a weapon that best fits the illrigger in their party. We suggest tying this weapon into a greater story, such as a power squabble in the Seven Cities, a feud between two fiends, or even a devil trying to learn your illrigger's true name—in Hell, a devil's true name can be spoken aloud to aid in summoning the fiend or to strip them of their power (see {@book Flee, Mortals!|FleeMortals} for these mechanics). Similar rules could apply to your infernal illrigger, if you wish.

Once a character claims {@i True Name}, they might quest to find its original name, thus learning the true names of many fiends in the hells and gaining great leverage. However, the weapon's wielder will undoubtedly encounter fiends who crave the weapon for themselves—such as Infernal Chancellor Lazivos, a chancellor in the Seven Cities whose agents collect powerful relics to enable his election to the Court. You can find his stat block and more information about him in {@book Flee, Mortals!|FleeMortals}!

name: Twinspawn Maulhammer
entries: {@i Component: aberration bone}
Made of the fossilised remains of a Deep One's spawn, the holes within this double-headed maul sparkle with illusory motes of light.

name: Tyrant's Talon
entries: {@i Component: Pouch of Dragon (Ophthalos) Claws}

"Who here wants a mighty blade forged from the talons of an ophthalos?" the guildmaster bellowed, and all intrepid adventurers across the taproom of the hunters' guild eagerly raised their hands. "And who wants to go kill one for the materials?" All of a sudden, there were no hands in sight.

entries.name: The Four Sacred Artifacts
entries: Four Sacred Artifacts appeared at the dawn of the Bürach Empire, each a divine gift from the four gods: Aurelia, Galt, Maligant, and Ulmyr. These relics were given to Bürach's first emperor, Indorius I, and inherited by each of his successors.

Maligant provided the mighty sword, Dämglesvir, to slay Bürach's enemies. Galt placed a crown on Indorius I's head to signify his divine right. Ulmyr gifted the emperor an orb of foresight to make him a wise ruler. Aurelia clad him in a breastplate, wishing only to protect him and his heirs.

Many centuries later, after Emperor Leopold I was assassinated, custody of the artifacts sparked a civil war. Each of the holy treasures disappeared amid the fighting. One religiously fervent tale claims they blazed with radiant light before banishing themselves beyond mortal reach. Other rumors suggest they were each stolen or lost in various separate conspiracies. It's certain that whoever holds the Sacred Artifacts controls the fate of the Bürach Empire.

entries.name: Wielding An Artifact
entries: Before disappearing, the artifacts were tarnished and corrupted by Emperor Leopold I's delusions, cruelty, and malice. Darkness had seeped into them, transforming their divine power and purpose. Though it's heretical to suggest, some believe the artifacts' befoulment is somehow linked to the death of the gods and the growing influence of the Great Beast.

Wielding even one Sacred Artifact is difficult. Their true power can only be unlocked by practicing their use. Yet this necessitates more time exposed to the darkness that now infuses them, which can infest the wielder's body and mind.

entries.name: Attunement and Proficiency
entries: Each Sacred Artifact has three tiers of {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB} available to its user. When a character attunes to the item, they have access only to the benefits (and the curse) listed under the Aspirant tier. The Adept and Master tiers of {@variantrule {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB}|XPHB} are unlocked over time (see Attunement Milestones, below).
{@variantrule Attunement|XPHB} to a Sacred Artifact can't be voluntarily ended. If the {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB} does end, the character can attune to the item again at the Aspirant tier.

Each artifact also curses its wielder. In addition to the curse effects listed for each tier, a character attuned to a Sacred Artifact is unwilling to part with the item, keeping it within reach at all times. If the artifact's curse is ended or suppressed, the character's {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB} with that item is broken.

entries.name: Attunement Milestones
entries: To ascend to a higher tier of {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB} and unlock additional powers of a Sacred Artifact, the attuned character must achieve a specific milestone. There is no minimum level required to achieve a milestone. However, Adept-tier artifacts are appropriate for characters of level 5 to 10, while Master-tier artifacts are appropriate for characters of level 11 and above.
The GM and players should work together to create appropriate milestones for the campaign, using these examples (themed to the four artifacts) as guidance:

items: Wield {@i {@item Dämglesvir|GrimHollowCG24}} to slay a mighty foe.
Take no damage during a difficult combat.
Earn the fealty of an important ruler.
You alter a future witnessed in {@i {@item Ulmyr's Eye|GrimHollowCG24}}.

entries.name: Shared Delusions
entries: The darkness that seeped into the Sacred Artifacts causes their wielders to experience the same paranoid delusions that plagued Emperor Leopold I.

All characters attuned to a Sacred Artifact suffer the same delusions, which could include the sense of being watched, believing a {@variantrule Friendly [Attitude]|XPHB|Friendly} NPC to be {@variantrule Hostile [Attitude]|XPHB|Hostile} , or mistaking an innocent person or household pet for a monster. Characters can even experience multiple simultaneous delusions.

A character suffering a delusion can use the {@action Search|XPHB} action to discern the truth, typically by succeeding on a {@dc 20} (or higher) Wisdom ({@skill Insight|XPHB} or {@skill Perception|XPHB}) check.

If the GM is using the {@variantrule Influence Dice|GrimHollowCG24|Influence Dice rules} rules, the frequency and intensity of delusions increases while the number of dice in the Beast Pool exceeds the number of dice in the Resolve Pool.

entries.name: Blessed Wisdom
entries: Religious texts claim Ulmyr plucked one of their own eyes as a gift for the first emperor. With it, Emperor Indorius I and his descendants would act with a measure of Ulmyr's foresight and wisdom.

The eye was kept inside the Sovereign's Orb, a golden reliquary inlaid with jewels mined from each of Bürach's provinces. These would remind the emperor of their duty to each of the realms they ruled.
The uncharged claw can be turned into a {@item galvanized claw|SGttEH} by crushing the live heart of a {@creature galvanized prowler|SGttEH} with it.

name: Undertaker's Cloak
entries: {@i Component: undead (mummy) rancid fat}

Mort I. Fiéd had learned one thing whilst under his father's tutelage; in this world, corpses don't always stay corpses. When the dead start rising, you want someone to have your back. Someone... or something.

name: Unmarked Grave
entries: {@i Component: undead ethereal ichor}

The phantasmal limbs that reach from the centre of this stone blade are eerily familiar to those who look upon its ethereal green depths. However, any morbid curiosity induced in observers is quickly curtailed by the frigid chill that emanates from the sword; the closer one gets to the weapon, the stronger the presence of the vengeful unresting who lurk on the other side of the shimmering rift.

images.credit: One of: Miguel Regodón Harkness, Marcel Mercado, William O'Brien, Sam Perin, Florian Stitz, Bryan Syme, Egil Thompson, Jon Pintar

name: Urchin Flail
entries: {@i Component: beast stinger}
A sphere of dark purple bristling with needle-sharp spines is connected to a driftwood shaft by a rusted chain.

images.credit: One of: Miguel Regodón Harkness, Marcel Mercado, William O'Brien, Sam Perin, Florian Stitz, Bryan Syme, Egil Thompson, Jon Pintar

name: Venus Fool's Trap
entries: {@i Component: pouch of plant leaves}

Brutal and unnatural magic can be used to transform a living plant creature into a garment. Made from a shapeshifting species of carnivorous plants, this red and green cloak pulses, moving around your body of its own accord. Yet the metamorphosis is far from perfect; this cloak constantly hungers for flesh.

name: Verdure
entries: {@i Component: fey (Bramble Queen) heart}

Oddly light and perilously sharp, these axes are often a first choice for pranksters and mischief-makers. Little can compare to the joy of watching a foe flail pathetically in the air before plummeting back to earth, or the satisfying crunch that often follows.

name: Vinecharmer
entries: {@i Component: Plant (Mosslax) Bark}
Snake charming is boring and cliché. Everyone's seen a dancing snake before. Now, making the petunias hop up and dance the tango? That's a novelty.

name: Viridian Deceiver
entries: {@i Component: pouch of dragon (green) scales}

This polearm embodies the treacherous, deceitful essence of the green dragon. Foul poison drips from its curved, golden blade, warning that beneath its beautiful surface, this weapon is just as dangerous and deadly as it is elegant.

name: Vitalophage
entries: {@i Component: ooze vesicle}

After years of study, frequently punctuated by time-consuming pranks, Humperdink and L'Arsène cracked the arcanical secrets behind how microorganisms turn living tissue into factories for more microorganisms. Adapting this process to a scale handleable by people, the pair created a blade capable of biological warfare. Delightful.

name: Voidshot
entries: {@i Component: aberration (beholder) main eye}
This jagged black, glass arrowhead drinks in light and seems lit as if with an unholy nimbus.

name: Wand of Acidsap Occlusion
entries: Should one manage to slay an {@creature acidsap gympie|TPK}, the creature's leaves and their acidic coating can be fashioned into a wand of acidsap occlusion. Doing so requires 60 hours of strenuous activity and a successful DC 23 Intelligence ({@item Alchemist's Supplies|PHB}) check. The creation of this wand may require additional components or a cost of 12,000 gp, at your discretion. When properly harvested the acidic leaves of a gympie can be sold for 3,000 gp to the right buyer. Rangers, druids, and some clerics who favor a wilderness lifestyle have learned that chewing the leaves results in a pleasant sensation that takes the edge off better than any ale.

name: Warhammerhead
entries: {@i Component: beast (giant shark) flesh}

Jealously guarded by mysterious keepers of the secrets of yore, the enigmatic instructions for creating this menacing weapon, staunchest ally to bloodthirsty pirates and ravenous ocean dwellers, are thus: take a shark head. Enchant it. Shove a stick in it. Yes, that's it. Did you expect more? It's a shark head on a stick.

name: Waspberry Jam
entries: {@i Component: phial of plant sap}

name: Waxen Sceptre
entries: {@i Component: elemental (pontiff) core of wax}

Sinister yet holy, the waxen god blesses those who endure their molten ministrations, restoring their fortitude, protecting their skin, and purifying their words. When lit, the candlesmoke of this sceptre carries the subtle, sweet scent of charred flesh while its tendrils form the screaming visages of those it has blessed.

name: Weave Stripper
entries: {@i Component: aberration tentacle}

Part trap, part torture device, part magic removal mechanism, the weave stripper is a gold-banded, lead-lined box that houses a portal to a remote, antimagical corner of the Abyss. The denizens of this void feed on the Weave, forcibly removing it from the creatures around which it is woven.

name: Weaveshaped Sword
entries: {@i Component: phial of humanoid (spellcaster) blood}

A book with a handle? How ingenious! Hold it between your thighs while you sunbathe, keep your greasy, post-sausage-roll fingers off its pristine pages, and, of course, turn the book into a crossguard spouting a blade of pure magic. This blade's high magical conductivity changes its nature in response to magical discharges and can drain power away from spellcasters it strikes.

images.altText: A sleek, silver dagger with a black, slender hilt and two raven feathers tied onto the pummel.

name: Willbow
entries: {@i Component: undead (will-o'-wisp) ethereal ichor}

Grown in fey soil, these wrought-iron bows are used by unseelie fey in conflicts against their Seelie cousins. Turquoise fruit sprouts from the metallic branches; bulbs of liquid fire ripe to erupt and scour the ground for a new generation of growth.

name: Wings of Chaos
entries: {@i Component: phial of fey blood}

Ever the chaotic mischief-makers, seelie fey hold unpredictability contests at deliberately irregular intervals, picking the winner at random, often from outside the registered competitors. The flutter of this blade's butterfly wings causes a series of unexpected events and exceptional outcomes. After winning several games in a row, the item was banned from all such competitions.

name: Wings of Prey
entries: {@i Component: pouch of beast (giant eagle) feathers}

Bestowed upon defenders of city walls and mountain rangers alike, these wings provide great mobility, as well as packing a secret weapon. The appearance of the wings varies from one individual to another, shifting in colour to mirror their soul.

name: Wings of the Hellspawn
entries: {@i Component: fiend skin}

The membranes of these wings are almost transparent in bright daylight, the bones appearing like fleshless claws. Come night or thick shadow, the membranes coalesce into blood-red curtains of opaque, ragged flesh. As you attune to this item, bands of sinew wrap around your form, binding you to these grotesque bone-and-membrane wings.

name: Winter's End
entries: {@i Component: bundle of plant roots}
Woven from the first branches to bloom at the end of winter, this living bow is strung with a length of snow-spider's silk.

name: Wishes 99
entries: Rumors of the legendary wheel come and go with the tides every few centuries. Some say it was once known as {@i Wishes 1121}, but its true origins have been lost to the depths.

name: Withercap
entries: {@i Component: pouch of plant spores}

Various little gourds and mushrooms constantly grow and die on the brim of this conical hat, each cycle of life and death taking only a matter of hours. Even in this decay, however, there is immense beauty, for it allows the old to fade away and gives way to a brand new arrangement of shapes and colours.

name: Worldshaper
entries: {@i Component: humanoid (dwarf) heart}

When gods still walked the world, dwarven smiths forged an axe to rival the powers of deities. With it, they carved a new world of rock; canyons sheared under its mighty blows, mountains were beheaded, and great stone caverns were founded where only impenetrable rock had stood before. Incensed by the dwarves' hubris, the gods cursed the axe and extracted promises from all dwarvenkind that they would never again reach for the power of the gods.

images.altText: Thick blood-stained cloth bandages affixed to two forearms. The wraps emit a red glow.

name: Xyxlbark Armour
entries: {@i Component: plant bark}

Armour made from the cured bark of the xyxl tree is stronger and lighter than steel and possesses the ability to nourish its wearer. The source of the xyxl tree's immense durability is the mithral particles it incorporates into a rigid lattice throughout its wood. The art of curing the slow-growing xyxl bark is known to but a few denizens of the Plane of Fey to which it is native.

name: Xyxlwood Arrow
entries: {@i Component: bundle of plant roots}

name: Xyxlwood Sporeshiv
entries: {@i Component: pouch of plant spores}

In the glimmering Plane of Fey, xyxl trees have one nemesis: the witherblight fungus. The hyphae creep through the trees' vascular systems, before blooming in one fungal explosion that turns the entire plant into a glowing, orange fruiting body. Clever sylvan craftspeople have developed a means of enchanting xyxlwood weapons to host this fungus and inject the necrotic spores under a pierced foe's flesh.
